question: How does a self-supervised model learn without human labels?
direct_answer: It trains on a target generated automatically from the input or from another sample in the dataset.
expanded_answer: A self-supervised pipeline defines a target signal from the data itself. For example, the model may predict a masked token, identify whether two views come from the same image, or align an input with a transformed version of itself. Since the target is constructed automatically, the model still receives a supervised-style loss even though no person annotated the data.
key_points: Training still uses a loss function
Can use same sample or paired samples
common_wrong_ideas: No labels means no target at all
The model just clusters data with no objective
